text: Create one focused Cambridge Stage 5 mathematics lesson: Rounding decimal numbers to the nearest whole number. Use the verified source notes in curriculumSource. One objective: round positive one-decimal-place numbers to the nearest integer and explain the decision using proximity and the halfway convention. Prerequisite: recognise tenths and adjacent whole numbers. Use original examples: a ribbon measuring 2.8 metres for the hook and worked example; a number line from 2 to 3 with mark 2.8; show distances to each endpoint in narration. Guided question: round 6.2 to the nearest whole number, followed by a separate explained answer (6). Misconception: 4.5 is exactly halfway; by the rounding convention used here it rounds UP to 5, not 4. Independent transfer: round 8.5 metres to the nearest whole metre, followed by a separate explained answer (9 metres). Briefly explain that rounding is approximation, not an exact equality: never write 2.8 = 3. Use rounds to or approximately. Required sequence: concrete hook, concept, worked example, guided question, guided feedback, misconception repair, independent question, independent feedback, recap. Each question reserves six seconds of silent thinking time, with no answer in its labels. Use meaningful number-line visuals for explanations and questions; use equation visual only for short feedback labelled rounds to. Avoid whole-number base-ten scenes, unrelated topics, bullet-heavy screens, broad decimal place-value detours, and copying textbook prose. All numerical examples described as original practice. Aim for 180 seconds, concise natural teacher narration, supportive pointing/focus supplied by approved renderer. Do not show Cambridge branding or claim Cambridge approval.

URL: https://www.cambridge.org/go/ereader/read/9781108964180/?groupId=0&bookid=2225&root=anon#book/2225/xhtml16 . Paraphrased scope: round numbers expressed to one decimal place to the closest whole number. Use number lines to compare distance to adjacent integers; tenths zero through four round to the lower integer, five through nine to the higher integer. The halfway case follows round-up convention for these positive numbers. Measurements retain units. The source uses worked examples, number-line identification, independent rounding, and correcting a mistaken halfway answer. This film is a bounded introductory lesson, not coverage of every exercise or every section of the book. All practice contexts and script should be newly authored.
